title: Rising and Falling Array Pairs
src: Media.net OA, IIT Patna. Coding question 2 of 3.
body:
For integers N and M, count the pairs of arrays (X, Y) such that:

  • both have length N and every element is between 1 and M;
  • X is non-decreasing and Y is non-increasing;
  • X[i] ≤ Y[i] for every i.

You get Q queries as two arrays A and B of length Q. Query i has N = A[i] and M = B[i]. Return every answer modulo 109 + 7.

Function to complete

Complete countArrayPairs(A, B). It returns the answer to each query, modulo 10^9 + 7.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: First line: Q. Second line: A[0..Q-1]. Third line: B[0..Q-1].
out: The Q answers on one line, separated by spaces.

spec.returns: the answer to each query, modulo 10^9 + 7

ref:
class Solution:
    def countArrayPairs(self, A: List[int], B: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        # X followed by Y reversed is one non-decreasing sequence of length 2N over 1..M,
        # so the count is C(M + 2N - 1, 2N).
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        top = max(m + 2 * n for n, m in zip(A, B))
        f = [1] * (top + 1)
        for i in range(1, top + 1): f[i] = f[i - 1] * i % MOD
        inv = [1] * (top + 1); inv[top] = pow(f[top], MOD - 2, MOD)
        for i in range(top, 0, -1): inv[i - 1] = inv[i] * i % MOD
        return [f[m + 2 * n - 1] * inv[2 * n] % MOD * inv[m - 1] % MOD for n, m in zip(A, B)]

wrong.why: counts X and Y independently, ignoring X[i] ≤ Y[i]
